paper.title: Mathematical Games: The fantastic combinations of John Conway's new solitaire game 'life'

headline: Conway Game of Life (deterministic cellular automaton): 2/3 locked clauses REPRO; glider period=4 translation=[1, 1], blinker/beacon period 2, block still life (period 1)

verdicts.gate: P1 glider is a period-4 diagonal spaceship (returns to its shape translated by exactly (+1,+1) after 4 generations)
P2 blinker period 2 AND block is a still life (period 1, unchanged)
P3 beacon period 2; live-cell count conserved for the block and oscillates with period 2 for blinker/beacon
reasons: measured blinker period=2, blinker count series=[3, 3, 3]; beacon period=2, beacon count series=[8, 6, 8]; block count conserved=True (need beacon period=2, block count conserved, and live-count period-2 oscillation for both blinker and beacon)

extra.model_class: deterministic cellular automaton (NOT agent-stepping ABM): a single synchronous B3/S23 transition is applied to the whole grid at once; there are no agents, no scheduler, no per-agent decisions and no randomness
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic CA result; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the catalogued EXACT periods/translation and would catch an artifact (e.g. a wrong rule giving the wrong period)

citations: Gardner, M. (1970). Mathematical Games: The fantastic combinations of John Conway's new solitaire game 'life'. Scientific American 223(4):120-123. doi:10.1038/scientificamerican1070-120.
Conway, J.H. (the B3/S23 rule and the glider/blinker/block/beacon catalogue, as popularized by Gardner 1970).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction. The catalogued Conway/Gardner pattern periods (glider 4, blinker 2, block 1, beacon 2) and the glider's (+1,+1) net translation are the literature anchors.
